pixelObservationBasis: One native-resolution open of each original PNG in one six-image batch; no reopens, crops, resets, candidate/template/draft or author-suggestion access. Retained SOURCE review was read once to bind prior approval, not used as this inventory.

figures.routingReason: The apparatus, charge marks and indicator geometry can be expressed schematically with deterministic geometry; no semantic raster artwork is necessary.

rawProseBindings.relationship: Initial charged electroscope with a metal disk on its stem; this is the before condition for fig-129.

inventory.description: One upright electroscope, shown from the front with a wide horizontal disk above a round enclosure and a stand below.

components.observation: One thin horizontal oblong metal-disk profile at the top; black outline, five visible cross-shaped positive-charge symbols inside.
A short vertical connection descends centrally from the disk into the top of the enclosure.
One large white circular interior surrounded by a heavy black round rim.
An internal near-vertical solid member runs from the top rim through the central junction toward the lower interior.
One solid oblique member slopes from upper right through the central junction toward lower left.
A fan of short unnumbered solid tick strokes lies in the lower-left interior, adjacent to the oblique member.
A central support descends below the round enclosure to a low broad base; two long feet spread toward lower left and lower right, with a short rear/up-right projection.

relativePositions: The charged disk is above and connected to the enclosure, not beside it.
The internal members meet near the middle; the movable member is visibly displaced toward lower left compared with the downward fixed member.
The scale remains inside the lower-left quadrant, not an external ruler.
The support and feet are below the enclosure.

localHolds.fact: Exact number of tiny unlabelled scale ticks
localHolds.reason: Native-resolution black strokes are too small to count unambiguously in this single allowed view. A fan of ticks is certain; no exact count is certified.
localHolds.scope: This fine-detail count only; do not remove the instructional scale.

figures.routingReason: A natural hand holds the slab in a meaningful position above the charged apparatus. If that natural hand is retained as artwork, its layer is semantic and every apparatus component, gap, charge glyph and indicator relationship must remain deterministic. This classification does not authorize artwork generation or paid fallback.

rawProseBindings.relationship: An uncharged thick-glass dielectric is brought close to the charged disk; the indicator lowers and charge redistributes between the leaf and disk.

inventory.description: One electroscope of the same type as fig-128, now with one hand-held long dielectric slab above its charged disk.

components.observation: A long thin outlined slab extends approximately horizontally across the upper portion, beyond the disk width; its right end meets the holding hand.
Two closely spaced rows of repeated charge glyphs occur on the slab. Cross-shaped and horizontal marks are visible; exact row-by-row polarity/count of these very small marks is a local HOLD.
One hand enters from the upper right and grasps the right end of the slab; thumb/finger contours surround the grip. The hand is not touching the electroscope disk.
One separate horizontal oblong disk below the slab, with five visible positive-charge crosses.
A visible white separation remains between the slab and disk; neither an electrical wire nor direct contact joins them.
A central vertical stem connects the disk to the top of the round enclosure.
One white circular interior with a heavy black rim.
One principal near-vertical internal member extends from the top toward the lower interior.
A second solid member is now close to vertical, meeting the central junction and extending slightly toward lower left; it is less displaced than in fig-128.
A fan of small unnumbered tick strokes lies in the lower-left interior.
A support below the round case descends to a broad left/right-spreading base with a short rear projection.

relativePositions: The slab lies above the metal disk, with a nonzero gap.
The hand holds the slab at its right end; no hand is present in fig-128.
The disk, stem, central interior junction and support are vertically stacked.
The moving member is close to the fixed member compared with fig-128.

lineStyles.chargeMarks: short crosses and horizontal strokes, not motion arrows

localHolds.fact: Exact glyph count and row-wise polarity of the tiny slab marks, including the grip-side region
localHolds.reason: Several small strokes merge with the outline and each other at native resolution; I do not certify a guessed positive/negative count or face assignment.
localHolds.scope: Do not claim source-fidelity approval for a candidate's exact slab glyph layout from this baseline alone.

localHolds.fact: Exact number of tiny unlabelled scale ticks
localHolds.reason: The scale is visible but its exact tick count is not confidently resolved in the one permitted view.
localHolds.scope: Fine-detail count only; preserve the scale and reduced deflection.

figures.routingReason: A circular model, two solid charge markers, a dashed diameter and exact labels/point relationships require deterministic construction.

rawProseBindings.relationship: Historical hydrogen-orbit account: central positive nucleus, one moving electron, and opposite points 1 and 2 used for a time-average symmetry explanation.

inventory.description: A single large solid circle has a filled nucleus near its center and a filled electron on its upper rim, slightly right of the top.

components.observation: One unbroken solid circular outline.
One solid black central dot, adjacent to +q=e.
One smaller solid black dot on the upper rim, adjacent to -e above.
Label 1 lies outside the upper-right intersection of the diagonal and circle; the intersection has no separate filled marker.
Label 2 lies outside the lower-left intersection; this intersection also has no separate filled marker.
A dashed oblique line runs from the lower-left circle intersection through the nucleus to the upper-right intersection.

relativePositions: Points 1 and 2 are opposite across the central nucleus on one diagonal.
The electron lies on the circle but not at either labelled diagonal endpoint.
The -e label is above the electron; +q=e is beside/below the nucleus.

figures.routingReason: The joined two-lobe schematic, positive/negative placement and chemical identities are exact semantic geometry and labels, not a naturalistic scene.

rawProseBindings.relationship: The source NaCl account assigns a positive sodium ion to the left charge center and a negative chlorine ion to the right, preceding the far-distance dipole abstraction.

inventory.description: One continuous horizontally elongated two-lobe closed contour, narrowed at its middle, contains a plus sign in the left lobe and a minus sign in the right.

components.observation: One continuous solid peanut-like contour; two rounded lobes join through a narrow waist.
One large plus sign sits inside the left lobe.
One large minus sign sits inside the right lobe.
Na is printed below the left lobe.
Cl is printed below the right lobe.

relativePositions: Na and the positive sign are left; Cl and the negative sign are right.
The two lobes share one outline rather than two disconnected circles.
The chemical labels lie below their corresponding lobes, not inside the waist.
futureAssertionIntents: one joined outline and two lobes

figures.routingReason: Two point charges, their separation segment and exact magnitude/sign labels require deterministic geometry.

rawProseBindings.relationship: Far from the source ion pair, the model is two equal-magnitude opposite-sign point charges separated by l, with overall zero net charge.

inventory.description: Two filled black endpoint dots are joined by one nearly horizontal solid segment, with l above and opposite-sign equal-magnitude charge labels below.

components.observation: One filled black dot at the left segment endpoint.
One filled black dot at the right segment endpoint.
One straight solid segment joins the two dots; it has no arrowheads.
Italic lowercase l sits above the middle of the connecting segment.
+|q| is below the left dot.
-|q| is below the right dot.

relativePositions: The positive charge is left and the negative charge right, consistent with fig-132.
The connecting segment terminates at the charge centers.
l denotes the endpoint separation, not an arrow direction or numeric 1.
futureAssertionIntents: equal absolute-charge magnitude and opposite signs

crossFigureRelationships.relationship: Same apparatus type and positive disk sign; slab/hand absent before and present above the disk after, while the moving member becomes closer to vertical. No discharge/contact is shown.
A single instantaneous electron position is followed by a twelve-position series around one central positive charge. Twelve position symbols are not twelve simultaneous electrons.
The left-positive/right-negative source identity is retained when the joined ion-pair outline becomes two point charges separated by l.
